title: Removal of the Fwd Cargo Door Surround Corner Fittings

ata.title: Fuselage Section 13 — Forward — Door Surround Structure

abstract: Removal of the four corner fittings at the forward cargo door cut-out, including the local removal of the cargo compartment lining and floor panels that give access to the fitting flanges.

sections.purpose: This task gives the procedure to remove the four corner fittings of the forward cargo door cut-out, for replacement or for access to the frame web behind them.
sections.job_setup_note: Put the aircraft in the maintenance configuration with the forward cargo door open on its maintenance stay and the door actuation system isolated. The cargo compartment must be empty and the loading system de-energised. Two people are needed for the lower aft fitting because the access is restricted and the fitting cannot be supported by one person alone. Have the protective covers ready before you disturb any fastener, because the frame web must not be left open to the compartment.
sections.procedure: 1. Make sure that the forward cargo door is open and that the maintenance stay is installed. 2. De-energise the cargo loading system and install the warning notice at the loading panel. WARNING: DO NOT DO THIS TASK WITH THE CARGO DOOR ON THE ACTUATION SYSTEM. THE DOOR CAN MOVE WITHOUT WARNING AND CAUSE INJURY. 3. Remove the cargo floor panels local to the door cut-out in zone 113. 4. Remove the lower shell lining panels in zones 113 and 115. 5. Clean the fitting flanges and the adjacent surfaces. 6. Do a detailed visual inspection of each fitting and record the condition before you remove anything. 7. Slacken the tension-head bolts EN567460-96 at the first fitting in the release order of table 1, a quarter turn at a time, and remove them with the plain washers AGS531516-6D. Keep the fasteners in a marked container. CAUTION: DO NOT USE A POWER TOOL TO REMOVE THE FASTENERS. THE FRAME WEB CAN BE DAMAGED IF THE TOOL SLIPS. 8. Support the fitting and pull it clear of the web assembly D5321003375416. 9. Do steps 7 and 8 again for the other three fittings. 10. Put a protective cover on each open fastener hole. 11. Do a detailed visual inspection of the exposed web area.
sections.close_out: Put the removed fittings in a marked container and identify them by position. Make sure that all the fastener holes are covered and that no tool or fastener is left in the compartment. Record the condition of the web assembly on the aircraft work card. Table 1 gives the release order and the residual torque check figure for the tension-head set; record the highest breakaway torque read on each fitting. If the fittings are not to be installed again in the same shift, apply the temporary protective treatment to the exposed faying surfaces.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. The corner fittings are attached with the alloy steel tension-head set and one release order and torque table apply, given as table 1.

safety_precautions: Put the warning notices in position at the cargo loading panel.
Make sure that the forward cargo door maintenance stay is installed.

title: Removal of the Fwd Cargo Door Surround Corner Fittings

issue.reason: Second release order and torque table added for the titanium fastener set, with the step split by fitting standard.

ata.title: Fuselage Section 13 — Forward — Door Surround Structure

abstract: Removal of the four corner fittings at the forward cargo door cut-out, including the local removal of the cargo compartment lining and floor panels that give access to the fitting flanges.

sections.purpose: This task gives the procedure to remove the four corner fittings of the forward cargo door cut-out, for replacement or for access to the frame web behind them.
sections.job_setup_note: Put the aircraft in the maintenance configuration with the forward cargo door open on its maintenance stay and the door actuation system isolated. The cargo compartment must be empty and the loading system de-energised. Two people are needed for the lower aft fitting because the access is restricted and the fitting cannot be supported by one person alone. Have the protective covers ready before you disturb any fastener, because the frame web must not be left open to the compartment.
sections.procedure: 1. Make sure that the forward cargo door is open and that the maintenance stay is installed. 2. De-energise the cargo loading system and install the warning notice at the loading panel. WARNING: DO NOT DO THIS TASK WITH THE CARGO DOOR ON THE ACTUATION SYSTEM. THE DOOR CAN MOVE WITHOUT WARNING AND CAUSE INJURY. 3. Remove the cargo floor panels local to the door cut-out in zone 113. 4. Remove the lower shell lining panels in zones 113 and 115. 5. Clean the fitting flanges and the adjacent surfaces. 6. Do a detailed visual inspection of each fitting and record the condition before you remove anything. 7. Identify the fitting standard before you touch a fastener: an aluminium-lithium fitting is attached with tension-head bolts EN567460-96 under plain washers AGS531516-6D, a titanium fitting with hexagon head bolts AES495354-07 under countersunk washers AES963502K7. 8. On an aluminium-lithium fitting, slacken the bolts in the release order of table 1, a quarter turn at a time, and remove them with the washers. CAUTION: DO NOT USE A POWER TOOL TO REMOVE THE FASTENERS. THE FRAME WEB CAN BE DAMAGED IF THE TOOL SLIPS. 9. On a titanium fitting, slacken the bolts in the release order of table 2, which starts at the outboard row and works inboard, and remove them with the countersunk washers. CAUTION: DO NOT APPLY THE TABLE 1 RELEASE ORDER TO A TITANIUM FITTING. THE THICKER FLANGE PRELOADS THE JOINT DIFFERENTLY AND THE FLANGE CAN BE BOWED. 10. Keep the fasteners of each fitting in a separate marked container. 11. Support the fitting and pull it clear of the web assembly D5321003375416. 12. Do steps 7 to 11 again for the other three fittings. 13. Put a protective cover on each open fastener hole and do a detailed visual inspection of the exposed web area.
sections.close_out: Put the removed fittings in a marked container and identify them by position and by standard. Make sure that all the fastener holes are covered and that no tool or fastener is left in the compartment. Record the condition of the web assembly on the aircraft work card. Table 1 gives the release order and the residual torque check figure for the alloy steel set, table 2 the same for the titanium set; record the highest breakaway torque read on each fitting against the table you used. Fasteners of the two standards must not be returned to a common container. If the fittings are not to be installed again in the same shift, apply the temporary protective treatment to the exposed faying surfaces.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Pre MOD-160142 aircraft carry aluminium-lithium fittings on the alloy steel tension-head set and use table 1; post MOD-160142 aircraft carry titanium fittings on the hexagon head set and use table 2. The two tables are not interchangeable and the fitting standard must be identified before any fastener is disturbed.

safety_precautions: Put the warning notices in position at the cargo loading panel.
Make sure that the forward cargo door maintenance stay is installed.
